judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain identification of the two Consultants, the Company and an effective date keyed to the last signature; nothing in it carries two meanings, though it defines "Consultants" collectively without saying how the two share anything.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.a then uses the singular "Consultant" and promises "twenty-percent (20%) of the Profits," so the collective definition here leaves open whether 20% is per person or shared, a mild tension rather than a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain soft, undefined commitments — "future consulting services to enhance the value for the sale" upon request, and reliance on a Jasper Port "scheduled for construction in 2023" — whose content and effect are not fixed anywhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative Sections 2.a and 2.b impose an unconditional 20% payment obligation with no requirement that any future services actually be rendered, so a party could argue the recital's services language is a condition the operative text omits (classic recital-versus-operative divergence), and Section 3's integration clause does nothing to resolve it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Profit" is defined as total proceeds less "reasonable expenses, holding costs and expenses relating to transactions regarding the property (i.e. donations, etc)" — "reasonable," "holding costs," and an "i.e. ... etc" catch-all that misuses i.e. for e.g. leave the deductible categories genuinely unbounded (general-vs-specific and vagueness both).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 2.a, which measures the Consultants' 20% by this figure, and with Section 2.b, where the same 100-acre donation is treated as a benefit generating shared tax savings while the definition apparently treats donations as a profit-reducing expense — a real risk of internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Consultant" appears in the singular against the two-person defined term "Consultants," and "[u]pon sale of a portion or all" leaves unclear how expenses and holding costs are allocated to a partial sale, so both the payee and the measure are arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends entirely on the elastic Section 1 definition of "Profit" and on the preamble's collective definition of "Consultants"; the mismatch between them is the kind of point a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Company or its principal may realize certain tax savings" is permissive and indefinite, "its principal" is undefined, and payment is triggered "once the risk of a federal or state tax audit has expired, which is expected to occur in October 2016" — an expectation, not a fixed date — with a comma splice joining the two sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 1, the donation is listed as an expense reducing "Profit" yet here generates a separate 20% entitlement, and the recital describes the donation as already completed with Consultants' assistance, leaving the timing and measure of this payment hard to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional merger clause; the only soft edge is the limiting phrase "in connection with Delta Bluffs," which confines its supersession effect but is not itself of two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the recitals in c002, which supply the only description of the consulting services and of the Jasper Port assumption; if one side relies on that background, the integration clause is the provision opposed to it, but the recitals are part of the same writing so the tension is limited.
